simple.meaning: דַּךְ (dak) is a Hebrew word meaning “crushed , i.e. (figuratively) injured.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: דַּךְ (H1790) appears 4 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Psalms 9:10, with occurrences in Psalms, Proverbs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to דַּךְ (H1790) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in דַּךְ (H1790) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: דַּךְ (dak) / H1790 is traced through Psalms 9:10, Psalms 10:18, Psalms 74:21, Proverbs 26:28 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H1790. dak דַּךְ adjective crushed, oppressed — דַּךְ Psa 74:21 ; דָּ֑ךְ 9:10 ; 10:18 ; plural suffix דַּכָּ֑ו Prov 26:28 (Baer; and other editions דַּכָּיו ) — in poetry; always figurative, oppressed, distressed Psa 9:10 Psalm 18 (|| יתום ) 74:21 (|| עָנִי and אביון ); Prov 26:28 דַּכָּו = those crushed by it (a lying tongue).
